id.description:
UUID v4 minted by the caller; the idempotency key. An audited request's id stays
deduplicated for as long as its audit row is kept (`audit.retention_days`, BUS.md §5.3).

payload.description: Op-specific; `{}` when the op takes nothing.

token.description: Session token binding an `agent:<name>` actor on the socket door.

Actor.description: "user" | "agent:<session-name>" | "test" | "system". "system" is the engine itself: it appears on events, audit rows and holds, and every door rejects a request that claims it

id.description: `null` only when the request could not be parsed far enough to read one (`bus.parse`).

replayed.description: Present (true) when the id was seen before and the recorded result was returned.

mail.description: Live, unaudited sideband. Present only when an authenticated agent has priority mail.

Response.description: A response envelope (BUS.md §1.2). Exactly one of `result` / `error` is present.

message.description: Human sentence; may change; never parse it.

Confirm.description: The op that lifts a hold (present iff `kind == held`).

priority.description: Number of unread priority messages for the authenticated agent session.

cause.description: Request id that caused it; absent for system-originated events.

Event.description: A fact about a mutation that already happened (BUS.md §1.3).

stream.description:
`pty` | `logcat` | `mirror`, all on the socket door (BUS.md §7). `app.log.tail` declares
a `log` stream but is not built: it sends no frames.

mirror_id.description: `mirror` only: which `device.mirror.start` this frame belongs to.

epoch.description: `pty` only: increments on every spawn/wake; `seq` restarts at 0 within it.

data.description:
base64 for `pty`; a line for `logcat`; for `mirror`, a base64 video packet or a status
object (state, picture size, device, and the typed reason on the last one).

Frame.description: A data-plane frame (BUS.md §7) as carried on the socket door.

implemented.description: Whether the running engine has a handler for it (else `bus.not_implemented`).

call.description:
All-layers verdict for the asking actor. `None` when nothing evaluated it (the static
schema render), so a reader never mistakes "not computed" for "callable".

why.description: Which layer decided `call`, in one phrase.

oneOf.description: `user` and `test` (and `system`).
Everyone may call it, but the op exists *for* agents (self-report style).

Doors.description:
Which doors carry an op. A `socket_only` op acts on the connection that sends it (a
subscriber, a wait), so the socket door answers it; the engine refuses it with `bus.door`.

oneOf.description: Callable as asked.
Refused before the handler runs.
Callable, but only for the actor's own session (or its PAIR partner, for reads).

Callable.description:
Whether the asking actor may really call an op, across all three gating layers
(registry `actors`, runtime row scope, and the role allowlist). `bus.ops` reports it.

can_call.description: Every op this actor may really call, all three gating layers applied.

write_roots.description: Absolute roots this actor may write to, worktree first.

events.description: Exact names or `prefix.*`. Empty waits for anything.

timeout_ms.description: How long to block before giving up. Default 60s, clamped to an hour.

matching.description:
Only an event whose payload has every one of these top-level keys equal to the value
given, e.g. `{"request_id": 7}`. Omit to take the first event that matches by name.
Anything but an object is `bus.schema`: read as "no filter", it woke on any event.

spawn_profile.description: How Relay spawns it: flags, env, hook file layout. Opaque, for display and diagnosis.

guarded.description:
Whether this provider supports Relay's `PreToolUse` guardrail and lifecycle adapters.
Provider-native trust may still require one explicit approval before a generated hook runs.

payload.description: `null` when the payload was larger than 64 KiB.

expect.description: `{updated_at}` of the entity after the op; `audit.undo` refuses on mismatch (§5.5).

orders.description: Every workspace whose `order` changes, each once. The rest keep theirs.

force.description:
Also remove every project in it, closing their open sessions (`project.remove` with `force`).
Without it the op refuses `workspace.has_projects`.

remove_worktrees.description:
With `force`: also delete the Relay-pool worktrees of the sessions it closes. Branches
are always kept; off by default, so every checkout stays on disk.

discard_changes.description:
With `remove_worktrees`: delete them even with uncommitted changes. Without it, a dirty
one is refused `worktree.dirty` before anything is closed or removed (RA-405).

orders.description: Every project whose `order` changes, each once. The rest keep theirs.

force.description:
Close its open sessions (`session.close`, worktree kept) and stop its device runs first.
Without it the op refuses `project.sessions_live` / `project.activity_live`.

remove_worktrees.description:
With `force`: also delete the Relay-pool worktrees of the sessions it closes. Branches
are always kept; off by default, so every checkout stays on disk.

discard_changes.description:
With `remove_worktrees`: delete them even with uncommitted changes. Without it, a dirty
one is refused `worktree.dirty` before anything is closed or removed (RA-405).

path.description:
The repository's new root: absolute, a git repository, no other project's path, and inside
a workspace (the project moves to the innermost one that contains it).

backup_path.description: The backup to pass to `project.restore`: the newest one that still holds the project.

A file in the store's `backups/` directory, as `project.removed.list` or the removal's
`project.deleted` event names it.

parent_id.description: Create it straight as a sub-task of this one; refused past `TASK_DEPTH_MAX`.

labels.description: Free-form tags; unknown names are created in the project's label set.

TaskState.description: Agent lifecycle on a task, independent of column (BUS.md §11.1, confirmed 2026-08-17).

TaskType.description:
A first-class classification, separate from the free-form `labels` (BUS.md §11.1).
`Task` is the neutral default and is what every pre-v16 row migrated to; the other four
are the vocabulary the board filters on.

module_name.description:
The name of `module_id`'s module, completed (archived) ones included, so a card can be
labelled without a `module.list` (RA-495). Absent from an older engine.

parent_id.description: Parent task, if this is a sub-task. Nesting is capped at [`TASK_DEPTH_MAX`] levels.

depth.description: 0 for a root task, 1 for its child, and so on — never above `TASK_DEPTH_MAX - 1`.

children.description: Direct children, in board order. Children stay real tasks with their own cards.

rollup.description: Progress over the whole subtree, for the parent's `n/m done` badge.

labels.description: Free-form tags, sorted; the supplementary layer under `type`.

blocked_by.description: Tasks this one waits on (stored edges).

blocks.description: Tasks waiting on this one (the inverse read of `blocked_by`).

duplicate_of.description: The task this duplicates, if any.

sessions.description: Every session ever dispatched to it, in order; a PAIR adds two.

TaskRollup.description:
Roll-up of a parent's descendants (BUS.md §11.1). Counts the whole subtree, not just the
direct children, so a grandparent reads as one body of work. Zero `total` = a leaf.

path.description: Path under the store's attachment dir.

comments.description:
Every comment on the task, oldest first; not paged. `task.comment` rows stay out of
`history`, so a comment is reported once.

TaskComment.description:
One entry in a task's discussion, GitHub-issue style. `author` is the session name for an
agent and `user` for a person, as `mailbox.send` renders `from`.

label.description: One label name, exact and case-insensitive.

session.description: A session name; matches every task that session was ever dispatched to.

parent_id.description: `Some(Some(id))` = children of that task, `Some(None)` = roots only, absent = every task.

limit.description:
Page size, default 1000, at most 2000. Done cards sort last, so a page cut short drops
the oldest finished work first.

offset.description: Skip this many tasks of the ordered result: the previous page's `next_offset`.

summary.description: Leave each task's `body` and `changelog` empty: a board needs titles, not essays.

next_offset.description: Set when more tasks match than this page holds: pass it as `offset`.

expected.description: Original editable field values; every supplied value must still match atomically.

parent_id.description: Absent or null detaches the task back to a root.

Label.description: A free-form supplementary tag, scoped to a project. Types classify; labels annotate.

TaskRelation.description:
Task-to-task edges other than parent/child (BUS.md §11.1). Only these two are stored;
`blocks` is the inverse read of `blocked_by` and never has a row of its own.

fanout.description: Also dispatch every not-done descendant, one fresh session each. Requires `create`.

start.description:
Defaults to true. False stages the assignment without starting the provider, so a
multi-task launch can attach its complete queue before the first agent turn.

worktree.description: `"new"` (default: pooled worktree), `"primary"`, or an absolute path of an existing worktree.

prompt.description: Persist the initial assignment before spawning, so a partial launch can recover it.

intent.description: One line of what this session is doing, in its own words (`session.intent`).

column.description: The column the task goes back to; not `done`.

position.description: Its 0-based index in that column, as in `task.move`.

state.description: The run state it had before the approval.

sha.description:
The commit link the approval created, removed again. Absent when the approval linked a
commit that was already there, which then stays.

project_id.description:
Required from the person; an agent may leave it out for its own project, the only one
it may name (D106).

expected.description: Original editable field values; every supplied value must still match atomically.

group_by.description: Only `"priority"`, the default; anything else is refused.

include_deleted.description: Also list soft-deleted notes (`deleted_at` set), which `notes.restore` brings back.

summary.description: Cut each `body` to a preview of its first 240 characters; `notes.get` has the whole note.

expected.description: Original editable field values; every supplied value must still match atomically.

expected_updated_at.description:
The target note's `updated_at` as you last read it. When given and the note has changed
since, nothing is appended (`notes.edit_conflict`); omitted, the text is appended as before.

delivery.description:
`queued` (at least one addressee is live), `session_parked` (all parked),
`not_running` (all created or exited), or `no_recipients` (an empty broadcast).

state.description:
The recipient session's state right now: `running` will see it, `parked` will not
until it wakes.

before.description: Only messages older than this message id: the previous page's `next_before`.

messages.description: Oldest first. Without `unread_only` this is the newest page; with it, the oldest unread.

next_before.description: Set when older messages remain: pass it as `before` for the page before this one.

more_unread.description: More unread messages remain past this page (`unread_only`): ack these, then ask again.

prompt.description: Omitted preserves the allocated assignment; an empty string explicitly clears it.

discard_changes.description:
Delete the worktree even with uncommitted changes (tracked edits or untracked files).
Without it, removing a dirty Relay-pool worktree is refused `worktree.dirty` (RA-405).

status.description:
`completed` (default), `blocked`, or `partial`. An op that can only report success
gets reported success (D118).

text.description: One line, present tense. Empty clears it.

paths.description: Worktree-relative paths this session is taking on.

symbol.description: Narrow the claim to one symbol within each path.

exclusive.description:
Refuse the whole claim if any path is already claimed by a peer, instead of recording
it alongside theirs and reporting the collision.

collisions.description: Peers already holding one of these paths. Empty is the quiet, expected case.

paths.description: Omit to release every claim this session holds.

intent.description:
One line of what this peer is doing, in its own words (`session.intent`). Coordination
needs to know what a peer is *up to*, which no amount of state and branch names says.

text.description: Everything, skills included. What the UI shows.

compact.description:
State, peers, notes and adjacent work only — the part small enough to inject on every
spawn. Skill bodies are referenced by path instead of inlined (D101).

task.description: Current task retained for older clients and one-task agents.

tasks.description: Current task followed by every queued or in-review task attached to this session.

assignment.description:
The launch prompt, on the session's first launch only: a relaunch may come long after
that work was done (RA-397). The brief keeps it as the original launch assignment.

brief_path.description: Worktree-relative path of the full brief.

peers.description: Everyone else live in this project, now.

can_call.description: Every op this session may really call, all three gating layers applied.

discovery.description: How to inspect operation summaries and exact payload/result schemas without guessing.

comms.description: How to reach the peers above, and which channel actually reaches all of them.

write_roots.description: Absolute roots this session may write to, worktree first.

dry_run.description: The op that answers "would this be allowed?" without doing it.

exceptions.description:
What to do when a refusal stands between you and the task: how to ask the user for an
exception and wait for the answer.

until_detach.description:
Borrow the size: on a connection door, the PTY goes back to the size it had when this
connection detaches from the session or goes away, unless someone resized it since.

cols.description: The live PTY's size; absent when the text comes from a saved scrollback.

project_id.description:
Only this project's sessions. Each one costs a `git status` of its worktree, so a
client describing one project's panes should not pay for every project's (RA-235).

discard_changes.description:
Delete the worktree even with uncommitted changes. Without it, a dirty Relay-pool
worktree that the discard would delete is refused `worktree.dirty` (RA-405).

verdict.description:
Always `allow`. A refusal arrives as a typed `refused` error and a hold as a typed `held`
error whose `confirm` names the hold, never as a verdict here (BUS.md §9.3).

error.description: Never set; a refusal is the response's `error`.

hold_id.description: Never set; a hold's id is in the `held` error's `confirm.payload`.

full.description:
Return every string whole, however large. By default a string over 64 KiB in the
payload or details is cut to its first 4 KiB and named in `elided`.

request.description:
The exact frozen action, with authentication material removed. `guardrail.confirm`
replays the stored action whole, whatever was elided here.

elided.description: JSON pointers (`/request/payload/new_text`, `/hold/details/reason`) of the strings cut short.

scope.description: Exception requests only: how long the grant lasts. Defaults to what the agent asked for.

GrantScope.description: How long an approved exception lasts: one use, or until the session ends.

workspace_id.description: One of the two, or neither for the global layer.

denied_commands.description:
Command patterns refused for `kind: exec`. Matched against the *parsed argv* of each
command in the line, never as a raw substring, so quoted data mentioning one is fine.

allowed_write_roots.description:
Absolute roots an agent may write to outside its worktree — scratch space, which is
not a repo-integrity concern. `$TMPDIR` is always honoured in addition to these.

agent_builds.description:
Whether an agent's `integration.request` may run the project's build command without a
person confirming it. Off by default: the build runs outside any sandbox (RA-167), so an
agent's request that builds is held for confirmation; a merge-only request is not.

GuardrailConfig.description: Effective guardrail configuration after global + project merge.

min_file_lines.description:
The percentage rule is skipped for files shorter than this. A percentage of a very
short file measures nothing: one line of a one-line file is 100%.

allow_if_recoverable.description:
Let a large rewrite through when git can put the file back — committed and unmodified,
or ignored entirely. Set false to hold on volume alone.

DestructiveWrite.description: A write is destructive when either threshold is exceeded.

ShapeGate.description: A built-in validator attached to one critical, worktree-relative path.

RoleAllowlist.description: Role allow-sets are configurable, but the defaults are the baseline in BUS.md §9.1.

workspace_id.description: Patch this workspace's layer. At most one of `workspace_id` / `project_id`.

patch.description: Merged into the layer's stored overrides; `null` clears a key back to the inherited value.

workspace_id.description: At most one of the two; neither reads the global layer.

inherited.description: What this layer would get with no overrides of its own: the parent layer's effective config.

overrides.description: This layer's stored overrides, exactly as stored.

sources.description: Leaf path (`caps.files`, `protected_paths`) to the layer that decided its value.

GuardrailLayer.description:
Which layer of guardrail configuration a value lives in. Each layer overrides the one
before it: defaults, then global, then the project's workspace, then the project.

paths.description: Worktree-relative paths the plan intends to touch.

lines.description: Lines the plan expects to change in total, if known.

commands.description: Commands the plan intends to run.

verdict.description: The worst verdict across everything below.

files.description: What the plan costs against the commit caps.

write_roots.description: Absolute roots the caller may write to.

policy.description: The policy that decided it, when one did.

kind.description:
`command` for a denied command, `path` for a protected path / write root / large rewrite,
`cap` for the commit caps.

value.description: The exact command line; the path (worktree-relative or absolute); or `files=N lines=M`.

reason.description: Why you cannot progress without it. The user reads this before deciding.

scope.description: What you are asking for; the user may grant less. Default `once`.

ExceptionKind.description:
What an agent asks to be let past. `command` lifts a denied command, `path` a protected
path, a write root or a destructive-write rule, `cap` the commit caps.

created.description: False when an identical request from this session was already open.

wait_for.description: The event announcing the answer; wait with `bus.wait {events:[wait_for], matching:{request_id}}`.

id.description:
Also the id of the hold that carries it, so `guardrail.confirm` / `guardrail.reject`
answer it with `hold_id` set to this.

value.description:
The exact command, the path (worktree-relative, a glob, or an absolute root), or the
caps wanted (`files=N lines=M`; empty lifts the caps for the grant's life).

active.description: Approved, not revoked, and (for `once`) not yet used.

GuardrailException.description: An agent's request to be let past one guardrail, and — once a person answered — the grant.

oneOf.description: Waiting for an answer.
Approved and still usable.

files.description:
A wholly untracked directory is one entry, its path ending in `/`. At most a few thousand
entries: conflicts first, then other tracked changes, then untracked ones.

truncated.description: Whether `files` stops short of every change git reported.

total.description: How many entries git reported, `files` included; more than `files.len()` when truncated.

staged.description: Compare with the index, what a commit would record, instead of the working tree.

old_path.description: For a rename, the file's path in the old side (`renamed_from` in `git.status`).

branch.description: The branch name on the remote, `feature`.

local.description: The local branch of the same name, if there is one; switching to the remote selects it.

name.description:
A local branch, or a remote-tracking one (`origin/feature`) to check out as a new local
tracking branch.

carry_changes.description:
Bring uncommitted changes to tracked files along, as `git switch` does. Git still refuses
when the target branch would overwrite them; nothing is ever discarded.

branch.description: The local branch now checked out.

created.description: Whether a local tracking branch was created for a remote branch.

refresh.description:
Ask GitHub now instead of answering from the last listing (kept up to a minute, and
dropped by `git.push` and `git.pr.open`). For an explicit refresh, not for every redraw.

failed.description:
Branches found merged that were not deleted (or, on a dry run, would not be), with why:
a dirty or still-held checkout, a rebase in progress, a failed delete (RA-373).

session.description: The closed session that worked on it.

reason.description: Why: how the work was found merged, or what unmerged work kept it.

merged.description: Its work was found merged; a `kept` row with this set is one cleanup could not delete.

limit.description: Most entries listed per directory, default 2000, at most 5000.

truncated.description:
Directories cut short at `limit`, by worktree-relative path, with how many entries each
really holds. Ask for one again with its `path` and a larger `limit` to see more.

worktree.description:
The checkout to put it back into (`@project` or a worktree path). Default: the one it was
deleted from, or the project's primary checkout once that one is gone.
The checkout it was put back into.

fallback.description:
Set when no `worktree` was named and the one it was deleted from is gone, so it went to
the project's primary checkout instead.

worktree.description: The checkout it was deleted from, and where `file.restore` puts it back by default.

available.description: Whether the trashed bytes are still on disk.

glob.description:
A glob without `/` (`*.rs`) matches the file name at any depth; one with `/`, or a
leading `/` to anchor it, matches the whole worktree-relative path.

col.description: 1-based byte offset of the match in the whole line.

text.description: The line, or for a long one a window of it around the match.

text_offset.description:
Set when `text` is a window: the byte offset in the line where it starts, so the match
begins `col - 1 - text_offset` bytes into `text`.

lease.description:
Who is using this device right now, if anyone. A conflicting run, install or claim
from anyone else is refused with `device.busy` until it is released.

device.description:
The device serial, or `*` when the command named no device (adb's only device, or
Gradle's every device): that lease conflicts with every device.

session.description: The holding session's name; `None` when the user holds it directly.

action.description:
What the holder is doing, in a few words (`device.run debug from relay/brisk-otter`,
`adb install app-debug.apk`).

expires_in_s.description: Seconds until the lease lapses on its own; `None` while it lasts as long as its run.

DeviceLease.description:
One holder's exclusive use of an Android device: a `device.run` in flight, an agent's
`adb install` / `gradlew install*` seen by the guardrail hook, or an explicit `device.claim`.
Released with a `device.lease.released` event, so `bus.wait` can wait for it.

kind.description:
`run` installs and launches on `device`; `build` produces an artifact and
leaves `device` empty (D152).

artifact.description: Absolute path of the APK / AAB a finished `build` produced.

variant.description: Gradle variant and artifact format for a release build; absent for device runs.

publish.description: True when this build was also handed to Gradle Play Publisher.

signing.description: `signed`, `unsigned`, or `unverified` after Relay inspects the artifact.

device.description: Serial from `device.list`; omit to claim every device (what a bare `adb` would touch).

action.description: What you will be doing, shown to anyone refused with `device.busy`.

minutes.description: How long to hold it. Default 10, at most 60; released early by `device.release`.

device.description: Serial to release; omit to release every lease you hold.

windows.description: Provider's own units and windows, opaque; the UI knows each provider's shape.

summary.description:
Cut each body to its opening, frontmatter included, instead of the whole SKILL.md;
`skill.get` returns one whole body.

description.description:
What the skill is for: the `description` of its SKILL.md front matter, else the first
line of prose after it; empty when there is neither. Read from the whole body, so it is
there even when `skill.list {summary: true}` cuts the body short.

source_ref.description:
The branch or tag a GitHub skill was installed from; `None` is the repository's
default branch (or a local skill). A refresh pulls this ref again.

Branch or tag to clone; overrides one named by a `tree/<ref>` URL. When neither names
one and `subdir` is an installed skill's `source_path`, its recorded `source_ref` is
kept, so "Update from GitHub" stays on the branch the skill came from.

replace_skill_id.description:
Explicit permission to replace one visible skill when its name conflicts with the
downloaded SKILL.md. Hidden soft-deleted rows are reclaimed automatically.

docs.description: Documentation files, relative to the plugin root; `plugin.get` returns their text.

enabled_in.description: Projects the plugin is switched on for.

suggested_for.description:
Projects whose checkout looks like this plugin's kind of project (for Unreal Engine, a
`.uproject` at the root) and that do not have it on yet.

Plugin.description:
A plugin bundled with Relay: skills, always-on agent instructions, documentation and MCP
servers that reach every agent of a project the plugin is switched on for (D159).

name.description: The skill's folder name, which is also its provider-visible name.

files.description: Files in the skill folder, `SKILL.md` included.

instructions.description: The instructions every agent of an enabled project receives in its brief.

count_only.description: Only `unread`: no rows are read and `notifications` comes back empty. For a badge.

unread.description:
Unread notifications matching `project_id` / `category`, however many `limit` and
`unread_only` leave out of `notifications` (RA-490). Absent from an older engine.

link.description: Deep link: an op to run when clicked.

PaneTarget.description: What a pane shows; shape depends on `PaneKind`.

today.description: The day to read the month from; today in the engine's time zone when absent.

empty.description: No accounts and no entries: draw the honest empty state.

recent.description:
The latest few entries, for Home. Left out for a model, which answered "the biggest expense"
from these few instead of the period's entries.

expected.description: What an even spend would have used by the end of today.

pace_delta.description: Positive when spending runs faster than an even pace.

days_left.description: Days still to spend in, today included.

daily_allowance.description: What can go out each remaining day and still land on budget. Zero once the budget is gone.

spent_fraction.description: Spent as a fraction of the budget; may exceed 1. Zero without a budget.

pace_fraction.description: Where the pace tick sits on the meter, 0..1.

left.description: What is still to spend: `budget` less `spent`, below zero once it is over budget.

pace_delta.description: Above zero when spending runs ahead of an even pace through the period.

line.description: Where it stands in words: "$88 over pace, $119 left", "$8 over budget, 21 days left".

registration.description: An investment account's tax wrapper; `None` on every other account.

AccountType.description:
`Investment` holds money put to work (a TFSA, an RRSP, a brokerage account); its value can be
updated by hand.

Registration.description:
How the tax rules see an `Investment` account (docs/INVESTMENTS.md). A field of the account,
not an account type of its own.

GoalKind.description:
What a goal measures.

- `Savings`: a pot filled by contributions, toward a target and an optional date.
- `Balance`: an account (or everything you own, net of what you owe) reaching an amount by a date.
- `Invest`: each month, money moved into investment accounts: a share of what came in, or a set amount.
- `Save`: each month, what is kept of what came in: a share of it, or a set amount.

MoneyTx.description: One entry as a client draws it, its account and category names joined in.

net_worth.description: Every unarchived account's balance added up, as money.summary's `net_worth`.

devices.description: Phones that sync with this ledger, the latest first.

period_offset.description: 0 is the current budget period, -1 the one before.

query.description: Matches the note, category or account in any case and alphabet.

periods.description: How many budget periods, ending with `period_offset`'s: 1 to 6 (24 by period). Default 1.

period_offset.description: The last period: 0 is the current one, -1 the one before.

category.description: Only this category, by name (any case).

cumulative.description: Running totals across weeks or days, for pace.

today.description: The day to read the current period from; today in the engine's time zone when absent.

MoneySeriesIn.description:
The question a chart asks. A chart keeps this, not its numbers, so it redraws when the ledger
moves.

oneOf.description: Income less spending.
One label per category, the largest first; each period is a series.
Week 1 is the period's first seven days; each period is a series.
Day 1 is the period's first day; each period is a series.
One label per budget period, oldest first; one series.

label_colors.description: Each label's category colour (Tally's palette index), when the labels are categories.

values.description: One value per label, minor units.

known.description:
By week or day, in the period still running: how many labels it has reached. Later ones
have not happened yet, so a running total stops here instead of going flat.

to_account_id.description: Transfers only: the account the money goes to.

amount.description: Zero or less removes the budget.

registration.description: Investment accounts only: TFSA, RRSP, FHSA…

institution.description: Where the account is held, e.g. Wealthsimple.

month_start_day.description: The day the budget month starts on, 1 to 28.

MoneySettings.description: The ledger's own settings, carried in a backup.

path.description: An absolute path on the PC.

kind.description: `backup`: a Tally backup, which replaced the ledger.

device.description: The phone's name, shown on the PC.

replace.description: The phone's first sync with this PC: erase the PC's ledger and take the phone's.

since.description: The cursor this PC returned last time; 0 the first time.

generation.description:
The generation this PC returned last time; absent the first time. When the PC's ledger
is no longer that one, the sync is refused with `money.sync_stale`, and the phone takes
the PC's ledger whole (`since: 0`, no generation, no changes).

changes.description: The phone's rows changed since its last sync, and its tombstones.

MoneyChange.description:
One row's change on the sync wire (docs/MONEY.md, "Sync"). `row` holds the table's fields in
camelCase, references as uids; empty for a tombstone.

cursor.description: Store it and send it back as `since` next time.

generation.description:
Store it and send it back as `generation`: it changes when this ledger is restored,
erased or replaced, and a device holding an old one must take the ledger whole.

changes.description: This ledger's changes the device has not seen.

replaced.description: This ledger was replaced by the device's.

applied.description: The device's changes taken, and those older than what is here or not placeable.

today.description: The day to value the portfolio on; today in the engine's time zone when absent.

as_of.description: The newest snapshot or price date the reading rests on.

income_12m.description: Dividends, interest and reinvested distributions over the 365 days ending today.

income_by_month.description: The same by calendar month, the last twelve, oldest first.

kinds.description: By kind of security, cash as `CASH`, largest first.

issues.description: What the reading could not square, in plain words.

MoneyPortfolio.description:
The portfolio as both devices read it (docs/INVESTMENTS.md, "The portfolio reading"). Money is
in the ledger currency; `*_bps` are basis points. Nothing here is stored or synced: it is read
again from the rows each time.

valued_on.description: The newest snapshot or price date its value rests on.

return_bps.description: The money-weighted return: yearly when `return_annual`, else over the stretch since `return_since`.

SecurityKind.description: What a security is, for the allocation by kind.

currency.description: The security's currency; `price` is in it.

fx_estimated.description: Some of its value or book was converted without a rate.

no_price.description: No price on or before today: its value is its book.

ActivityType.description:
What an investment activity did. The order is normative: activities on the same day apply in
this order, then by uid, so a buy and a sell on one day never oversell.

over_taxed.description: What is over past the RRSP's $2,000 buffer; all of `over` for the others.

deadline.description: The last day that counts for the year.

MoneyRoom.description:
A registration's room in `year`: the CRA figure (`room`, `None` when none was entered) minus
what went in over the window that ends on `deadline`.

MoneyActivity.description:
One investment activity as a client draws it (docs/INVESTMENTS.md), its account and security
joined in. `quantity` is at 1e-8 of a unit; `amount` and `fee` are minor units of `currency`.

symbol.description: The security, e.g. XEQT; it is made when the ledger does not know it yet.

amount.description: Minor units of `currency`, never negative: the type says which way the money went.

to_amount.description: `FX` only: what the money became, in `to_currency`.

path.description: An absolute path on the PC: a Wealthsimple holdings report, activities export or monthly statement (CSV).

account_id.description: A statement names no account: the one it would go into, so lines already there count as duplicates.

MoneyImportPreview.description:
What importing a Wealthsimple file would do, before it does it. `new` and `duplicates` count
its holdings and activities: a duplicate is a line already imported (or imported and deleted).

MoneyImportKind.description: Which of the three files it was.

MoneyImportPreviewAccount.description: An account a Wealthsimple file names, and the Tally account already holding its number.

MoneyImportSkipped.description: A line the reader left out, and why. Lines count from 1 at the header.

path.description: An absolute path on the PC.

accounts.description:
Where each of the file's accounts goes, by Wealthsimple's account number: an `account_id`,
or a new account when it has none. A number not listed goes to the account already holding it.

account_id.description: A statement only: the account it belongs to.

MoneyImportAccount.description: Where one Wealthsimple account goes: `account_id`, or a new account when it has none.

MoneyImportResult.description:
What an import wrote. `duplicates` are lines it left out because they were already in (or
deleted); `skipped` lines it could not read.

amount.description: The person's figure from CRA My Account (or the Notice of Assessment for an RRSP), minor units. Zero or less removes it.

price.description: At 1e-8 of the security's currency's major unit: 3812000000 is 38.12.

base.description: ISO 4217 codes: `rate` is units of `quote` for one `base`, at 1e-8.

started.description: False when a fetch is already on its way.

provider.description: `claude`; the agent that answers in this thread.

effort.description: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`; the provider's default when absent.

working.description: The agent is writing a reply.

live.description: The agent is running for this thread now, so a new message costs no resume.

preview.description: The start of the last message, for the thread list.

after.description: Only the messages stored after this message id.

role.description: `user`, `assistant` (text and tool calls), `tool` (a tool's answer) or `error`.

text.description: The first message; the thread is named after it and the agent starts on it.

model.description: A model for this thread's agent; the provider's default when absent.

effort.description: How hard it thinks: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`; the default when absent.

model.description: The agent's model; empty or absent for the provider's default.

effort.description: The agent's effort; empty or absent for the default.

models.description: The models a thread may run on this PC, besides the provider's.

running.description: The local model the server runs now, if any.

idle_minutes.description: Minutes unused before the server stops; 0 never (`threads.local.idle_minutes`).

server.description: The `llama-server` that runs them; absent when it cannot be found, with `server_error`.

id.description: The model id a thread stores and the picker sends.

present.description: The file is in the models folder, so the model can run.

model.description:
The model picked: a local one starts loading, anything else (or none) stops the local
model server.

limits.description: Today's use of the Arbiter-wide limits.

checked_at.description: The runner's last pass, RFC 3339, and what went wrong in it.

ArbiterSummary.description: The Arbiter overview: the panel and the page draw from this one reading.

state.description: `none` (no key saved), `ok`, or `error` (the last check failed; see `error`).

key.description: The key's name with its middle hidden: `organizations/…/apiKeys/9a2e…`.

fees.description: The account's fee rates; the entry tier until a key reads the real ones.

ArbiterConnection.description: The exchange connection as last checked.

portfolio_uuid.description: The portfolio the key is limited to.

ArbiterPermissions.description: The key's permissions as the exchange reports them.

ArbiterFees.description: The account's fee rates, as fractions: 0.006 is 0.6%.

value.description: Cash plus holdings at the last price, home currency.

pnl_today.description: Strategies' profit today, realized plus open, after fees.

balances.description: The exchange's balances (live only; paper holds cash and strategies' positions).

ArbiterAccount.description: One venue's money: paper's simulated account or the exchange's real one.

ArbiterVenue.description: Paper simulates fills on real prices; live sends orders to the exchange.

value.description: Its worth in the home currency, when a price for it was found.

ArbiterBalance.description: One currency held on the exchange.

doing.description: What it is doing now: "Waiting for RSI(14) below 30", "Holding: sells at +4%".

pnl_realized.description: Realized profit after fees, quote currency.

pnl_open.description: What the holding is up or down at the last price, after the fee to sell it.

currency.description: The quote currency its amounts are in.

ArbiterStrategyRow.description: A strategy as a list row.

ArbiterGranularity.description: A candle's width, as the exchange names it.

oneOf.description: The rules place orders within the limits; an agent may only propose.
An agent may place orders itself, within the limits. Needs limits.
Every order, from the rules or an agent, waits for the person.

ArbiterRunState.description: Running, stopped by the person, or halted by a limit or the kill switch.

unit.description: How to show the numbers: `money`, `count` or `percent`.

ArbiterLimitUse.description: A limit and how much of it today has used.

title.description: One line: "Change the take-profit", "Buy 50 CAD of ETH".

outcome.description: What approving it did, or why it failed.

side.description: Orders: the side, amount and pricing.

draft.description: Strategies: what it would be, and its changes from now as sentences.

draft_hash.description: The fingerprint approval binds to: the draft approved is the draft shown.

ArbiterProposal.description: Something waiting for the person: an agent's suggestion, or an order in "every order asks".

ArbiterDraft.description: A strategy's name, product, bars, rule and limits: what a proposal would make it.

buy.description: How much to buy each time, in the product's quote currency.

ArbiterRule.description: A strategy's rule: when it buys, how much, and when it sells.

oneOf.description:
A scheduled buy (dollar-cost averaging), in UTC: `weekday` 1 (Monday) to 7 for `week`,
`day` 1 to 28 for `month`.
Buy when the condition holds on a closed bar and nothing is held.
The bar's close.
Simple moving average of closes.
Exponential moving average of closes.
Wilder's relative strength index, 0 to 100.
Percent change of the close over `bars` bars: 5 is +5%.
Highest high of the `bars` bars before this one.
Lowest low of the `bars` bars before this one.

ArbiterOperand.description: A value a condition compares: the price, an indicator over the strategy's bars, or a number.

oneOf.description: Below or equal on the bar before, above on this one.
Fills at once at the best price on the other side; pays the taker fee.
A post-only limit at the best price on this side; pays the maker fee, may not fill.

trailing_pct.description: Sell when the price falls this far below its highest close since the buy.

max_bars.description: Sell after this many bars whatever the price.

when.description: Sell when this holds on a closed bar.

ArbiterExit.description: When a strategy sells what it bought. Percentages are of the average buy price.

max_order.description: The most one order may spend.

max_position.description: The most held at once, at cost.

daily_loss.description: A loss today (realized, plus what open positions are down) that halts until restarted.

cooldown_minutes.description: Minutes to wait after a losing sell before buying again.

ArbiterLimits.description: What may never be exceeded. Absent means no limit. Amounts are the quote currency.

error.description: The exchange's reason, when it failed.

oneOf.description: Sent, not yet acknowledged as open.

ArbiterOrderStatus.description: An order's state on the exchange.

pnl.description: Sells: the profit it realized after fees.

ArbiterPrice.description: A price to show beside the strategies.

break_even_pct.description: The move a round trip needs to break even at the account's fees, percent.

variants_tried.description: How many versions of this rule have been backtested.

backtest.description: The latest backtest of this version.

equity.description:
Profit after fees over time, `[unix seconds, quote currency]`, at most 400 points. For the
chart; a model is not given it.

break_even_pct.description:
What a round trip costs in fees and slippage, percent: the move a trade needs to break
even.

start.description: Unix seconds, the first and last bar.

return_pct.description: Percent, after fees, on the most in the market at once.

max_drawdown_pct.description: The largest fall from a high, percent.

won_pct.description: Percent of closed trades that made money; absent with none closed.

buy_hold_pct.description:
Buying at the first bar's open and holding to the last close, percent, after one taker
fee each way.

deployed.description: The most in the market at once, quote currency.

reason.description: Why it sold; absent while still held at the end.

pnl.description: After fees, in the quote currency; open trades are marked at the last close.

days.description: Days since its first order there.

return_pct.description: Profit over the most it held at once, percent.

ArbiterRecord.description: A strategy's record on one venue.

ArbiterDecision.description: One line of the decision log: what a strategy decided, and why.

quote.description: Only products quoted in this currency, e.g. CAD.

query.description: Matches the product id or base currency.

price.description: The last price, when the exchange gave one.

tradable.description: False when the exchange has trading, or new orders, turned off for it.

ArbiterProduct.description: What a tradable product allows, from the exchange.

bars.description: How many bars back from now, up to 1500. 300 by default.

strategy_id.description: Mark this strategy's paper and live trades.

ArbiterSeries.description: A chart's numbers: candles and the trades made on them.

ArbiterMarker.description: A buy or sell on a chart.

strategy_id.description: Backtest this strategy's rule; or give `draft` to try a rule that is not saved.

days.description: How many days back, up to 730. 180 by default.

tuned_fraction.description: The fraction of the range the rule was tuned on; the rest is judged. 0.67 by default.

id.description: Absent creates a strategy (stopped, on paper, rules mode).

running.description: Start or stop it. A halted strategy needs `arbiter.restart`.

strategy_id.description: A strategy's limits; absent sets Arbiter-wide ones from `global`.

max_exposure.description: The most held across every strategy, at cost, in the home currency.

daily_loss.description: A loss today across every strategy that halts them all.

price_band_pct.description: How far from the best price a limit may be placed, percent.

slippage_pct.description: Slippage assumed for market orders in backtests and paper fills, percent.

approval_minutes.description: What a pending approval waits before it expires, minutes.

home.description: The currency totals are shown in.

paper_cash.description: What paper trading starts with, in the home currency.

reset_paper.description: Erase every paper order, fill and record, and start paper over.

strategy_id.description: One strategy; absent halts everything (the kill switch).

failed.description: Orders that could not be cancelled, and why.

strategy_id.description: A change to this strategy; absent proposes a new one.

why.description: Why, in a sentence or two the person reads on the card.

quote.description: Buys: how much quote currency to spend.

base.description: Sells: how much base to sell; absent sells what the strategy holds.

limit.description: A post-only limit at the best price instead of a market order.

outcome.description:
`placed` (the gate passed and it went to the venue), `proposed` (waits for the person:
the strategy is not in "AI trades within limits", or every order asks) or `refused`.

draft_hash.description: Approvals bind to what was shown: the proposal's `draft_hash`.

imported.description: Absent until an export was imported.

weeks.description: The last 12 weeks, oldest first, this one last.

streak_weeks.description:
Weeks in a row with a workout, counting back from this week (or last, while this one is
still empty).

records.description: The newest eight lifts Avex marked as records, each with its best set that day.

lifts.description: The lifts done most in the last 12 weeks (all time when none were).

exported_at.description: As Avex wrote it: the phone's local date and time.

imported_at.description: RFC 3339, when the PC read it.

days_per_week.description: Avex's training days a week, 0 when unset.

lifts.description: The lifts done, in order; skipped ones left out.

untracked.description: Excluded from Avex's stats, and from every total here.

GymRecord.description: A lift's best set: by estimated one-rep max, the heavier on a tie.

best.description: The best set ever, by estimated one-rep max.

recent_e1rm.description: The best estimated one-rep max of the last 28 days.

change_pct.description: That beside the best of the 28 days before, in percent.

target_key.description: What it is about: a lift's id, a measure.

target_value.description:
A `lift_target`'s weight is in the person's unit like every other weight; any other
kind's figure is as Avex stores it.

limit.description: At most this many; 50 by default, 500 at most.

lift.description: Only workouts with this lift (a unique part of its name is enough).

id.description: The session's id, as the lists give it.

was_pr.description: Avex marked a personal record on it.

kind.description: `work`, `warmup`, or Avex's own name for another kind (`drop`…).

best.description: The exercise's best set by estimated one-rep max.

query.description: Only lifts whose name contains this.

name.description: The lift's name as Avex shows it; a unique part of it is enough.

limit.description: At most this many sessions, newest first; 100 by default.

top_weight.description: The heaviest working set's weight and its reps.

record.description: Its e1rm beat every earlier session's.

limit.description: At most this many, newest first; 50 by default.

by.description:
`week` (default), `month`, or `session` (one point per session; with a `lift`, each session
it was done in).

periods.description:
How many weeks or months end at the current one; for `session`, how many weeks back. 12 by
default, at most 260.

lift.description: A lift by name, as Avex shows it; a unique part of the name is enough.

GymSeriesQuery.description: What [`series`] reads. Every field is optional.

lift.description: The lift's name as Avex shows it, when one was asked for.

unit.description: What the values are in: `kg`, `lb`, `sessions`, `sets`, `minutes` or `km`.

values.description: One per label; null where there is nothing to read (a week without that lift).

path.description: An absolute path on the PC.

exported_at.description: As Avex wrote it: the phone's local date and time.
